XXVIII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|371}}</noinclude>receiuing vs, for three daies intreated vs courteou{{ls}}ly. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=8}} And it chaunced that the father of Publius lay vexed vvith feuers and the bloudy flixe. Vnto whom Paul entred: and vvhen he had praied, and impo{{ls}}ed hands on him, he healed him. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=9}} Vvhich being done, al in the ile al{{ls}}o that had infirmities, came, and vvere cured: {{verse|chapter=28|verse=10}} who al{{ls}}o honoured vs vvith many honours, and when vve vvere {{ls}}ailing away, laded vs vvith nece{{ls}}saries.

{{verse|chapter=28|verse=11}} And after three moneths, we {{ls}}ailed in a {{ls}}hip of Alexandria, that had wintered in the iland, vvho{{ls}}e {{ls}}igne vvas the Ca{{ls}}tors. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=12}} And vvhen vve vvere come to Syracûsa, vve taried there three daies. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=13}} Thence compa{{ls}}sing by the {{ls}}hore, vve came to Rhegium: and after one day the South winde blovving, vve came the {{ls}}econd day to Putéoli, {{verse|chapter=28|verse=14}} vvhere finding brethren, vve were de{{ls}}ired to tarie vvith them {{ls}}euen daies: and {{ls}}o vve came to Rome. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=15}} And from thence, vvhen the brethren had heard, they came to meete vs vnto ''Apij-forum'', and the Three-tauerns. Vvhom vvhen Paul had {{ls}}een, giuing thanks to God, he tooke courage. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=16}} And vvhen vve vvere come to Rome, Paul vvas permitted to remaine to him {{ls}}elf with a {{ls}}ouldiar that kept him. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=17}} And after the third day he called together the cheefe of the Iewes. And vvhen they vvere a{{ls}}{{ls}}embled, he {{ls}}aid to them, Men brethren, I doing nothing again{{ls}}t the people, or the cu{{ls}}tome of the fathers, vvas deliuered pri{{ls}}oner from Hieru{{ls}}alem into the hands of the Romanes, {{verse|chapter=28|verse=18}} who vvhen they had examined me, vvould haue relea{{ls}}ed me, for that there vvas no cau{{ls}}e of death in me. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=19}} But the Ievves contradicting it, I vvas compelled to appeale vnto Cæ{{ls}}ar, not as hauing any thing to accu{{ls}}e my nation. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=20}} For this cau{{ls}}e therfore I de{{ls}}ired to {{ls}}ee you and to {{ls}}peake to you. for, becau{{ls}}e of the hope of Israël, am I compa{{ls}}sed vvith this {{sup|‖}} chaine.

{{verse|chapter=28|verse=21}} But they {{ls}}aid to him, Vve neither receiued letters concerning thee from Iewrie, neither did any of the brethren that came hither, report or {{ls}}peake any euil of thee. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=22}} But vve de{{ls}}ire of thee to heare vvhat thou thinke{{ls}}t: for {{sup|‖}} concerning this {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ αἱρέσεως.}}∷ {{ls}}ecte, it is knowen to vs that it is gaine{{ls}}aid euery vvhere. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=23}} And vvhen they had appointed him a day, they came to him vnto his lodging very many: to vvhom he expounded, te{{ls}}tifying the kingdom of God, and v{{ls}}ing per{{ls}}ua{{ls}}ion to them<noinclude>{{rh||Aaa ij|of}}</noinclude>
